sentences.text: For Appellants : Mr.F.Terry Chella Raja  in all appeals  For Respondents : Mr.J. Michael Visuvasam for R2  in all appeals  R1  Ex parte  in all appeals  COMMON JUDGMENT Challenging the Award and Decree passed by the Tribunal, the claimants preferred these appeals.

2.The learned counsel appearing for the appellants/claimants would submit that without considering the permanent disability, the Tribunal erroneously awarded compensation as per percentage, as such, is erroneous and liable to be set aside.
3.With regard to the contributory negligence, based on the complaint, the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent raised objections stating that the Tribunal https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
has rightly awarded compensation by taking into consideration the injuries sustained by the claimants which needs no interference.
Further, he would point out that at the time of accident, three persons have travelled in the two wheeler and the rider of the two wheeler did not possess a valid driving license.
Due to their negligence, the accident has occurred and therefore, they also contributed to the negligence.

Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly fixed the contributory negligence at 15% on the part of the rider of the two wheeler, is correct for the reason that at the time of accident, the rider did not possess a valid driving license to drive the vehicle.
According to the respondents, they crossed the road suddenly so that the accident has occurred.
Further, the Rough Sketch was not produced before the Tribunal.
4.Considering the submissions made on either side, the claimants have also contributed to the said accident.
Three persons have travelled in the two wheeler at the time of accident.
Therefore, the contributory negligence of 15% fixed by the Tribunal on the side of the rider is valid one.

In M.C.O.P.No.781 of 2018, with regard to disability, the Medical Board assessed 40% of disability for the injuries sustained by the claimant Janaki on her spinal card, both side chest ribs, left hand and grievous internal injuries on her chest and the claimant suffered with permanent disability.

According to the respondents that there https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
10/07/2025 08:49:08 pm ) C.M.A.Nos.1965, 1940 and 1501 of 2023 was no such evidence adduced for the permanent disability and they were under the prolonged treatment, the objections raised by the respondents, is sustainable.
Therefore, 40% of disability is converted into the whole body, as submitted by the respondents.
Hence, Rs.7,000/- per percentage of disability is fixed by this Court.
The accident has occurred on 09.11.2018.
Therefore, the monthly income of the claimant is fixed at Rs.15,000/- per month.
In all other respects, the Award remains unaltered.
The enhanced compensation would be a sum of Rs.5,20,911/-.
